TEXT
Solar energy is transforming the way Tunisia produces electricity. In the last decade, the cost of solar panels has fallen by more than 80%, making them affordable even for small farms and households. Large solar plants have been built in the south of the country, where sunshine is abundant almost all year round. Supporters argue that solar power could make Tunisia energy-independent within twenty years, reducing its reliance on imported fuel. Yet challenges remain: panels must be maintained regularly, and the electricity grid needs upgrading to handle the new supply efficiently. Still, most experts agree that the country is moving firmly in the right direction.

1) What is the main idea of this text, in one sentence? (2 marks)
2) What tone does the writer use? Justify with one expression from the text. (2 marks)
3) What is the writer's purpose in this text? (2 marks)
4) Find one sentence in the text that uses the passive voice and explain why the passive is used there. (2 marks)

Read the text, then answer the questions.

TEXT
Youth unemployment remains one of Tunisia's most serious challenges. Every year, thousands of graduates leave university with strong qualifications but struggle to find a first job that matches their skills. Many end up accepting positions far below their level, while others choose to emigrate in search of better opportunities abroad. Economists warn that this waste of talent slows down the country's development and discourages young people from investing in further education. Some solutions have been proposed, such as closer cooperation between universities and employers, and support for young entrepreneurs who want to start their own businesses. Without urgent action, however, the problem is likely to grow worse rather than better.

1) What is the main idea of this text? (2 marks)
2) What tone does the writer adopt towards the situation? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
3) What is the writer's purpose: to inform, to entertain, or to warn and propose solutions? Explain. (2 marks)
4) Give a synonym from the text for "get worse". (1 mark)

TEXT
The new recycling centre opened in March with great fanfare: officials cut a ribbon, journalists took photographs, and the mayor promised it would "transform waste management in the city." Six months later, only one of the three sorting machines is working, and residents report that collection trucks often skip entire streets. The centre's manager says that spare parts have been ordered but have not yet arrived. Meanwhile, the amount of recyclable waste sent to landfill has barely changed since the centre opened.

1) What can you infer about the gap between the opening ceremony and the centre's actual performance? (2 marks)
2) What is the writer's likely attitude towards the officials' promise? Justify using evidence from the text, without quoting a full sentence. (2 marks)

Write a formal report (about 150 words) recommending improvements to public transport in your town, following the structure: Title, Introduction, Findings (two headings), Recommendations, Conclusion. Use the passive voice at least twice and avoid any informal language.

Read the text, then answer the questions.

TEXT
For centuries, the Mediterranean has been a bridge between cultures rather than a barrier. Traders, scholars and travellers crossed it constantly, carrying goods, ideas and inventions from one shore to another. Today, migration across this sea is often described only in terms of crisis and danger, and the human stories behind the numbers are easily forgotten. Behind every statistic is a person seeking safety, opportunity or simply a better future for their children. This does not mean that migration raises no real questions - it does - but framing it solely as a threat prevents thoughtful conversations about fair and workable policies. A more balanced narrative, neither naive nor alarmist, is urgently needed.

1) According to the text, how was the Mediterranean traditionally seen? (2 marks)
2) What criticism does the writer make about how migration is discussed today? (2 marks)
3) What is the writer's purpose? Is the text more informative or persuasive? Justify. (2 marks)
4) Identify the tone of the last sentence and explain what it reveals about the writer's stance. (2 marks)

Read the following short text, then answer the questions on main idea, tone, purpose AND transform one sentence into the passive voice - this combines all the skills of this chapter, as in a real Bac exam.

TEXT
Examination stress affects almost every student preparing for the Bac. Long hours of revision, family expectations and the fear of failure combine to create considerable pressure in the months before the exam. Teachers and psychologists increasingly recommend structured revision timetables, regular breaks and enough sleep, arguing that a rested mind performs far better than an exhausted one. Cramming the night before an exam, they warn, does more harm than good. Students who plan their revision calmly, rather than panicking at the last minute, tend to achieve better and more consistent results.

1) State the main idea in one sentence. (2 marks)
2) What is the tone: alarmed, reassuring-and-practical, or mocking? Justify. (2 marks)
3) What is the writer's purpose? (2 marks)
4) Put into the passive: "Teachers and psychologists increasingly recommend structured revision timetables." (2 marks)
